How to Prepare Your Skin Before Video Calls, Pitches and Recorded Videos
People see your face during pitch meetings, sales calls, investor updates and videos you post. Tired looking skin can affect the first impression people form of you.

You do not need filters or many products. Three things affect how skin looks on camera. Those are even skin tone, skin hydration and how evenly light reflects off the skin. Using one serum every day can help with hydration and tone.
What the camera actually sees

Camera sensors increase contrast. Dry skin reflects light unevenly, so shadows appear stronger in fine lines and the face can look more tired than it does in person. Hydrated and smooth skin reflects light more evenly. That even reflection is what people mean when they describe skin as looking bright and healthy.
The routine to use before a call, two minutes
Morning:
cleanse, then 2–4 pumps of PDRN Brightening Serum over face and neck. Let it absorb for a minute before moisturizer or sunscreen.
Five minutes before a big call:
splash cool water, pat dry, and press a half pump of serum onto the cheekbones and forehead, where light hits the face first.
Weekly:
use the same routine each week. Using the serum every day is what changes how skin looks on day 30 compared with day 1.
Why a serum, specifically

A serum is a concentrated liquid product applied to skin. The PDRN Brightening Serum contains PDRN and acetyl hexapeptide 8 with sodium hyaluronate, glycerin and panthenol. These ingredients add water to skin and help skin hold water. The serum is light, absorbs quickly and can be worn under sunscreen or on its own.
You prepare your slides, your numbers and your talking points before a pitch. Preparing your skin is part of preparing your appearance. The serum takes two minutes to apply.
